summary.text: Brenton Awa, a Republican Hawaii state senator for District 23 (Windward and North Shore Oahu), lost the November 3, 2026 election for U.S. House in Hawaii's 2nd District to Jill Tokuda.
First elected to the state Senate in 2022, he is the Senate minority leader and a former television journalist.

paragraphs.text: Awa was born in Ka'a'awa, Oahu, on February 19, 1986, and raised in Kahalu'u, and he graduated from Kahuku High School in 2004. According to Wikipedia, he earned a degree in speech communication and leadership from Clarion University of Pennsylvania (now Pennsylvania Western University - Clarion), where he wrestled.

Wikipedia says he began his television news career in 2009 at KGMB in Honolulu and joined KITV as a reporter in 2015, later serving as morning and evening anchor. Hawaii News Now describes him as a former television journalist.
Awa won election to the Hawaii State Senate in November 2022, defeating incumbent Democrat Gil Riviere 51.3 to 48.7 percent, and was re-elected in 2024 over Ben Shafer, 52.7 to 47.3 percent.

He has served as Senate minority leader since 2024 and sits on the Agriculture and Environment, Commerce and Consumer Protection, and Judiciary committees (2025-2026). According to his campaign website, his Senate work includes intervening in a state plan to raise rents for Waiahole farmers, creating roadside food forests in Kahalu'u and Hale'iwa, and passing a bill through the Senate to ban foreign ownership of agricultural land.
Awa announced his run for Congress in October 2025 while keeping his Senate seat, whose term runs to 2028, and ran unopposed in the August 8, 2026 Republican primary.
During the campaign, he said he would serve only one term in Congress, and his campaign said it was focused on housing affordability and restoring Hawaii's federal influence.
He received 33.5% of the vote to Jill Tokuda's 66.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

sources.title: Republican state senator confirms decision to run for Congress
